title: Colom wins Mississippi's Senate race after a long count
caption: Democrat Scott Colom, a district attorney, was projected Wednesday to have defeated Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith after officials spent days processing absentee and affidavit ballots; Hyde-Smith conceded by video that evening. Colom will be Mississippi's first Black U.S. senator since Reconstruction, and the result flips a deep-red seat. The magnolia, Mississippi's state flower, is symbolic.

stories.name: Democrat Scott Colom defeats Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi
facts: On Wednesday, Nov. 11, the AP, NBC News and CBS News projected that Democrat Scott Colom, a 43-year-old district attorney, had defeated Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi's U.S. Senate race.
The race was extremely close after Election Day; local officials spent several days processing absentee and affidavit ballots before the call, and Colom's narrow lead grew as counting went on.
Hyde-Smith conceded Wednesday evening in a video message, congratulating Colom. He will be Mississippi's first Black U.S. senator since Reconstruction.

artwork.alt: Editorial illustration. At night, election workers at a long green-covered table under desk lamps hold up and sort ballot envelopes, with trays of envelopes in front of them, while a worker in the foreground carries in another tray. Behind them, the Mississippi State Capitol, with its dome, lantern and gilded eagle, glows in front of a giant cream magnolia blossom that sends out rays of light. It represents the days-long count in Mississippi's Senate race, won by Democrat Scott Colom.
